long_biography.plain_text:
When Bulgaria's transition to a market economy created demand for modern machinery, Boryana Radeva and Dimitar Ilchev saw an opening. They started Euromarket in 1992 as a tool-supply company with fewer than ten employees, a small Sofia office, several telephones and one computer. The company expanded product line by product line into construction machinery, industrial equipment, compressors, vehicles, rental and technical service.

Radeva became the group's co-founder and general manager, pairing supplier relationships with a focus on trained sales and service teams. She remained an executive director and beneficial owner as the enterprise adopted holding structures and broadened its regional footprint. In 2026, a new board assumed direct leadership of Euromarket Group, while Radeva continued as a shareholder and representative within the private holding network behind its stake.

uncertainties: Identity is resolved at very high confidence through the exact full name, Bulgarian geography, Euromarket founder role and matching corporate filings. A Luxembourg-based European Investment Bank manager, a Coca-Cola corporate-services employee and a Sofia information-technology teacher share the shorter Boryana Radeva name but have incompatible careers and are excluded.

The source record's Boryana Georgieva Radeva form matches Bulgarian corporate filings and is retained. Some English transliterations use Boriana, but no evidence supports replacing the saved public form or dropping the patronymic.

No reliable source reviewed supplies an exact birth date, birth year or birthplace. Bulgarian birth country, nationality, residence, female gender and Alive status already exist in the immutable record and are not reproposed.

The direct personal wealth mechanism is not inferred from an executive title. Radeva's founder status is independently documented, and current corporate data identifies her as a 33.94% shareholder and beneficial owner of R I KO, the owner of ABG Hold, which is connected to a 50% Euromarket Group stake. Exact current look-through valuation and distributions are not public.

Service is the closest shared industry label because the group distributes, rents, installs and services machinery rather than manufacturing the equipment. Construction & Engineering was considered, but it would overstate the company's role as a contractor or producer.

Primary Industry uses the origin-sector fallback at medium confidence. Radeva's wider holding network includes property, river travel and other assets, but public evidence does not rank those interests against the retained Euromarket platform or establish Diversified as the principal current basis of her wealth.

Self-made is supported by the directly documented founder-built business and its growth from a small tool supplier. The public record does not establish the source of seed capital, prior family wealth, industry networks or other starting advantages, so neither self-made subtype is forced.

Founder remains current because Radeva retains an economic interest in the wealth-producing platform through the holding structure. Her direct Euromarket Group board and representative roles ended in July 2026, so the dossier does not call her the current operating group's chief executive or day-to-day operator.

Corporate records show Anton and Georgi Radev alongside Boryana and Ivan Radev in the holding structure, but no unsourced kinship label is used. The biographies refer only to a private holding network and a new management team rather than asserting exact family relationships or a transfer mechanism.

Heavy equipment is the single minimum useful governed tag because construction machinery and industrial equipment define the long-term founder platform. Automotive distribution, rental, property and shipping are either subordinate operating lines or broader holding interests and are withheld to avoid documentation-driven overtagging.

The official Euromarket site is proposed as the company website. No exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok, Wikipedia or personal website met the verification threshold, and no Forbes social is proposed because no dedicated profile exists.
Personal vessel facts, live company revenue and capital figures, unverified family relationships and speculative net-worth estimates are excluded from both biographies.

review.notes:
Terminal resolved-person dossier. Boryana Georgieva Radeva is the Bulgarian co-founder who helped build Euromarket from a small 1992 tool supplier into a construction- and industrial-equipment distribution, rental, engineering-support and service group. Founder ownership and personal economic interest are directly supported by current R I KO shareholding and holding-company roles, not inferred from employment. The dossier distinguishes the July 2026 operating-board transition from her continuing founder-shareholder relationship. Service describes the distribution and technical-service business model; Primary Industry uses a disclosed origin-sector fallback because the relative value of newer property, shipping and other holdings is not public. Self-made remains broad because the founder mechanism is clear but the pre-launch starting platform is not. No research has been compiled or applied.

Owner-tag consolidation research context: [1] Heavy equipment: Construction machinery and industrial equipment distribution, rental and service are the defining businesses Radeva co-founded and led. [2] Euromarket Group: Radeva co-founded the company and served as a general manager and executive director for decades; the named company is not an active approved tag. [3] Industrial equipment distribution: This is the precise operating model, but no active approved literal tag represents it separately from Heavy equipment. [4] Equipment rental: Rental is a documented business line but is subordinate to the wider distribution-and-service platform and lacks a stronger separate current cohort case here. [5] Technical service: Trained service teams, maintenance, installation and engineering support are core differentiators but remain operating detail rather than a separate literal assignment. [6] R I KO / ABG Hold: These structures establish current ownership and beneficial interest but are not proposed as tags. [7] Leadership transition: Radeva left the Euromarket Group board in 2026 while retaining holding-company roles; this is dossier analysis, not a taxonomy concept.
